recentItems.title: Israel intensifies strikes in southern Lebanon
recentItems.description:
WARNING: This story contains images which some viewers may find confronting. 

More than 13 people have been killed in southern Lebanon as Israel intensifies strikes in its self-declared "security zone".

The Israeli military has vowed to continue targeting Hezbollah, saying the latest wave of attacks were in retaliation to explosive drones launched towards its occupying forces.

Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun has labelled it a "dangerous escalation" which could jeopardise a US-brokered ceasefire that has been in place since June.

For more news: https://bit.ly/3qBhrgi

recentItems.title: Multi-agency operation targeting Australia's illegal tobacco trade
recentItems.description:
Nearly 2 million illicit cigarettes and vapes have been seized across the Northern Territory and Western Australia as federal agencies attempt to break the businesses’ model of illegal tobacco in Australia. 

Border Force led the week-long operation targeting distribution channels, but experts say not enough is being done to protect vulnerable people in the Top End.

SBS NT Correspondent Josh van Staden has more from Darwin.

recentItems.title: Protestors demand justice for Zomi Frankcom
recentItems.description:

Protesters have staged a dramatic demonstration outside the Israeli embassy in Canberra, demanding justice for killed Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom.

They called for Israel’s ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman to be expelled.

SBS Political Correspondent Rayane Tamer has the details.

recentItems.title: India’s sewer workers exploited by a system that treats them as ‘untouchable’
recentItems.description:
For generations, the task of cleaning sewers, septic tanks and drainage systems in India has traditionally fallen on marginalised Dalit communities.

India officially outlawed caste-based discrimination when its new constitution took effect in 1950.

The task of cleaning sewers without proper safety equipment was banned in 1993, but human rights groups say the practice continues, and that governments at all levels are using outsourced work and contractual labour hiring to skirt the law and deny responsibility for exploited workers.

International Correspondent Aaron Fernandes reports from New Delhi.

recentItems.title: Proposed social media legislation aims to give users more control over their feeds
recentItems.description:
Australian internet users will be given the choice to opt out of algorithmic recommendations under proposed social media reforms.

Draft laws setting up a digital duty of care were introduced by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on Tuesday.

As part of the measures, social media companies will need to provide tools for people to choose what they see in their online feeds, under a government initiative called My Feed, My Way.

Social media companies have been accused of creating addictive algorithms that keep people endlessly scrolling through recommended content. Advocates have called for a reversion to chronological feeds that show posts from friends and other accounts a user follows.

"This is not about giving government control. It's about giving people control. It's about putting choice back into the hands of Australians online," Albanese told reporters in Canberra.

Read more: https://bit.ly/4ytnAsL

recentItems.title: The unexpected way China is accused of exerting influence in the Pacific
recentItems.description:
Palau's president has accused China of 'weaponising tourism', after geopolitical tensions between the countries reignited.

The Chinese government warned its residents not to travel to the Pacific Island, a tactic historically believed to punish Palau for its recognition of Taiwan.

Now, Australia is trying to support tourism in the region, including doubling peak-season flights to help Palau attract more visitors and boost resilience.

recentItems.title: Who is Germany's AfD party? And what do they stand for?
recentItems.description:
The Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, putting the far-right party on the cusp of power at state level.

The party wants to heavily restrict immigration, restore ties with Russia, quit the euro and promote unashamed German patriotism.

While the AfD did not secure enough votes to win an absolute majority in parliament, the wider political significance of the election, which saw turnout over 80 per cent, according to broadcaster ZDF, was clear.

Read more: https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/germanys-far-right-party-tops-regional-election-for-first-time-since-worl-war-two/hj3r3bij5

recentItems.title: Far-right election victory in Germany| US envoys visit Ukraine | India building collapse
recentItems.description:
Germany's AfD has claimed victory in a regional election, marking the first win by a far-right party in the country since World War Two. 

The Alternative for Germany party secured about 44 percent of the vote in the east German state of Saxony-Anhalt. 

The result falls short of an outright majority, but the party believes it has won a mandate to govern.
